scope_registration_precondition: Root must independently accept this Source and register CP370/OW174 before constructing an actual request or running the caller.

future_scope_fields.source_hdf_ref: Root pins sealed HDF by exact path, sha256, bytes
future_scope_fields.source_mf_ref: Root pins sealed MF by exact path, sha256, bytes
future_scope_fields.caller_ref: Root pins this exact v5 Source caller
future_scope_fields.root_contract_ref: Root pins this exact v5 contract
future_scope_fields.before_canonical_refs: ordered exact three-key CP369/OW173/SS/CM39 refs, captured before CP370 registration; used only against Root-owned historical archive bytes
future_scope_fields.authorized_output_root: new caller-specific Root-owned output root within W09-99 receipts

cycle_rule: Scope binds historical CP369 Canon refs, accepted Source refs and expected revision numbers only. It does not bind CP370's own hash, its current Canon vector, registration proof or future Root request.

future_source_review.actor_id: must equal scope.source_reviewer and differ from source actor and Root

canonical_owner_worker_registration.CP_path: workers exact one row with step_id W09-99 and slice_id C19_MAIN_TWO_DISPATCHERS
canonical_owner_worker_registration.source_handoff_ref: same exact v5 Source HDF ref
canonical_owner_worker_registration.source_review_ref: same exact accepted Source review ref
canonical_owner_worker_registration.output_root: same caller-specific output root as scope and both docs

future_request_fields.scope_ref: exact three-key ref to Root scope-registration.root.json in current CP370
future_request_fields.current_canonical_vector_ref: exact three-key ref; refs array ordered checkpoint/path_ownership/step_state/commands, checkpoint_revision 370, path_ownership_revision 174
future_request_fields.current_owner_ref: exact three-key ref; owner_id Root, scope_ref, selected_worker_id Root; Owner document is sealed before Worker to avoid a reference cycle
future_request_fields.current_worker_ref: exact three-key ref; worker_id Root, scope_ref, selected_owner_ref
future_request_fields.historical_cp369_archives: ordered exact three-key refs to S369/historical.cp369.checkpoint.json, historical.cp369.path_ownership.json, historical.cp369.step_state.json, historical.cp369.commands.json; each byte-equal to corresponding before_canonical_ref
future_request_fields.output_dir: new absolute child directory of scope.authorized_output_root; must not exist

owner_worker_order: Root seals Owner first with selected_worker_id, then Worker with selected_owner_ref, then Root request with both exact refs; no Owner/Worker hash cycle.
owner_worker_canon_binding: Root CP370 and OW174 must each carry exact active lease, unique W09-99/C19_MAIN_TWO_DISPATCHERS binding to the OwnerDoc and WorkerDoc refs. Standalone documents alone cannot authorize execution; missing, expired, duplicated or conflicting active leases are rejected.
registry_selection: Dispatcher auto selects v2.4 only when pinned current_spec.json pointer and v2.4 commands.json plan_sha256 both equal the frozen plan. No explicit --spec is added to frozen C19 templates.
sealed_source_input_rule: Before any process launch, current CM39 registry, dispatcher source, locked toolchain, current_spec pointer, router, closure, Python executable and frozen plan must equal their exact refs in this Source MF's sealed source-input-pins.json. A newly calculated hash alone is not sufficient.
receipt_revision_binding: Each actual dispatcher receipt must independently report v2.4 registry, dispatcher, toolchain and W09 router hashes equal to the held Source pins; child_exit_code is read as an exact integer independently of the outer job's actual_exit.
verified_output: Each successful route produces a new route.verified.json containing the pinned actual dispatcher receipt; all output remains Root-owned and pending independent review.
historical_canon_read_rule: Native prepare/closed embedded CP369 Canon refs are checked against four Root-owned S369 historical archives. Current CP370 Canon refs are checked separately through the new consumer vector. Old CP369 hashes are never demanded from current Canon files.
